title.narrative: Final disposal solution identified and proposed

description.narrative: Final disposal solution identified and proposed

comment.narrative: Legislative framework regarding siting and licensing of radioactive waste management disposal facilities developed. Regulatory requirements in the field of radioactive waste management updated Clearance of radioactive waste regulation developed Treatment and conditioning regulation updated etc.. Basic Design Documentation that describes the selected disposal option and related techniques including the main features and functions of the waste package buffer and barrier materials developed.

Task 5 is anticipated to begin in mid2023 with definition of specific scope and schedule of implementation. A workshop with disposal experts and other relevant stakeholders will be held during 2023 to collect and discuss existing information and documentation and to define a scope compliant with the Description of Action and the allocated budget. It is envisioned that this workshop is needed to evaluate the appropriateness of the allocated budget for the required scope. Preliminary discussions on this matter has identified budget constraints for the completion of the full scope of this task mainly because the costs for the more prioritised tasks related to the storage facility monitoring programme development of legal and regulatory framework have increased and may have been originally underestimated. The output of the workshop may result in request for supplementary funds or reduced scope. The duration of the activities can be assessed as 55 months.

This task was presented and discussed during the meeting in Chisinau in May 2024. Developing a final disposal programme is a time consuming and costly activity and lesson can be learnt for example from Sweden even though Moldova does not have any spent nuclear fuel that needs storing. In the coming year a Statement of Work SoW will be developed for procurement of a supplier for a national screening of suitable regionssites for siting of a nearsurface disposal facility and deep borehole solution. The activity includes establishment of a working group SSM RWMCo and relevant Moldovan experts single firm procurement of an international expert and development of SoW.A deliverable is planned to be ready for review in mid 2025 and will be the basis for continued work. This task was presented and discussed during the meeting in Chisinau in May 2024 therefore it was highlighted that task 5 is overly optimistic in terms of scope time and funding given experience from similar work on a final disposal programme in Sweden.The next activity is related to the preparation of an application for additional EU funds to cover for the following steps as well as rescoping of task 5.

comment.narrative: The Terms of Reference for tasks 2 4 and 8 were finalized early in the year but the 2024 target to start procurement for the storage facility was not met due to SSMs lack of experience in building procurement. In agreement with Sida it was decided that another partner would handle the procurement. After a May meeting in Chisinau stakeholders agreed to assess the procurement capacity of the General Inspectorate for Emergency Situations GIES under the Ministry of Internal Affairs MIA. Ernst Young conducted this assessment in August and their October report indicated good procurement capacity with some improvement recommendations. SSM and Sida have since prepared changes to the Grant Arrangement to allow delegation of procurement responsibilities. Additionally SSM has worked on updating the MoU and PFA with MIA.
